lobby_en: Acre: a dark river map with wide crossings
loading_en: Acre is located in the extreme west of Brazil. The map is inhabited by the colorful Guarani and the Caribs and will probably never let you run out of wood, as the rainforest is dense. There are no gold mines; Acre is Brazil's greatest national producer of rubber and thus is very rich on rubber trees, which will provide you with the coin you need. Tapirs will be your main source of food. One of Amazon's tributaries separates the two teams from each other. Walkable crosses can be found on the shores of the river, and securing those is the key to victory, while its Fish can be a secondary food source.

loading_en: Also known as Asia Minor, the Anatolian Peninsula has experienced countless wars throughout the course of history. The Order of Christ has now sent some of their knights to build encampments there; forging an alliance with them will provide you with powerful units to expand your strategy. lobby_en: Araucania: fight along the western coast of South America.
loading_en: Araucania runs the length of South America's west coast and has plentiful hunting, fishing and whaling. Republiqueta towns occupy this variable landscape of mineral-rich northern deserts, bountiful central grasslands, and treasure-laden southern wastes.

lobby_en: Atacama: Salt mines are located in the middle of this map.
loading_en: The driest non-polar desert in the world, Atacama features no natives, as the conditions and the climate don't really benefit life. A few guanacos can be found scattered in the oldest desert on earth—as it is considered by many—while trees are only a few, as well. The map is, however, rich in salt mines, especially in the middle of it, where players cannot build anything due to the "salares", the salt lakes that dominate this area. Taking control of the Trade Routes that cross the center of the map is important, as they can keep you fed, when the rest of the resources have run out.

lobby_en: The remote west coast of the island that will one day be renamed Tasmania.
loading_en:
In the remote wilderness of Van Diemen's Land, the battle will be to control the only safe harbour on the rugged coastline.
The British colonial government have established a Convict settlement on an island in the middle of the harbour.
The Convicts are a good source of cheap labour.
The mainland is covered in dense forests of tree ferns and mighty mountain ash trees.
The only natural sources of coin on the map are the abundant Whales out to sea.

lobby_en: Yellow River: Offers extra resources and choke points when flooded, but is open and fertile when dry. Trade Routes on each side of the map, and many natives.
loading_en: During the dry season, the waters of the Yellow River recede to create fertile new islands, and animals often gather near the river's edge to drink. During times of flood, extra resources abound and naval craft are sometimes seen along the river. Recruit local groups as allies to take advantage of their multiple trade routes located along the borders of the map.

lobby_en: Yucatan: dense jungles and nearby natives.
loading_en: The Central America rain forests are home to many Treasures. Each player will start with a nearby Zapotec or Maya village. Use your ships to control the land on your side, or try to build a dock on the far shore and control both coasts.\n \nThe dense forests mean you will never run short of wood, and herds of Tapir and Capybara offer unusual hunting opportunities.

lobby_en: Snowy forests, plenty of silver, and sometimes a river.
loading_en: Your enemy's towns are close, so be on your guard. Cross the central river and claim the Treasure-rich region to the north. Mines are plentiful on the northern half of the map; expect to struggle until you have a second town.\n \nThe Trade Route will be hard to completely control, with each team having access to one Trading Post site. Two Cree or Nootka villages are found north of the river.
